subject: English
q: By its function, the sentence “I wonder whether he will come.” is:
o: Declarative
Interrogative
Imperative
Exclamatory
explanation: Although it contains an indirect question, the sentence itself is a statement and ends with a full stop, so it is declarative.

subject: English
q: By its function, the sentence “Never leave your luggage unattended.” is:
o: Declarative
Interrogative
Imperative
Exclamatory
explanation: It gives a (negative) command, so it is imperative.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is a subordinate clause?
o: the river is rising
the bridge collapsed
we took another road
because the bridge collapsed
explanation: A clause beginning with a subordinating conjunction such as “because” cannot stand alone.

subject: English
q: Which of the following groups of words is an independent clause?
o: when the river flooded
The river flooded the village
after the heavy rain
flooding the village
explanation: Only the first has a subject and finite verb and can stand alone as a sentence.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is a phrase, not a clause?
o: in the middle of the night
because it was dark
the night was dark
when the night fell
explanation: A phrase has no subject–finite verb pair; “in the middle of the night” is a prepositional phrase.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The committee approved the budget.”
o: The budget was approve by the committee.
The budget is approved by the committee.
The budget was approved by the committee.
The budget had been approved by the committee.
explanation: The simple past active becomes “was/were + past participle” in the passive.

subject: English
q: Change into passive voice: “They are building a new hospital in the town.”
o: A new hospital is being built in the town.
A new hospital is built in the town.
A new hospital has been built in the town.
A new hospital was being built in the town.
explanation: The present continuous passive is “is/are being + past participle”; “by them” is usually omitted.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Someone has stolen my bicycle.”
o: My bicycle has stolen.
My bicycle has been stolen.
My bicycle was being stolen.
My bicycle had been stolen.
explanation: The present perfect passive is “has/have been + past participle”; an indefinite agent (“someone”) is dropped.

subject: English
q: Change into passive voice: “The teacher will check the papers tomorrow.”
o: The papers will have been checked by the teacher tomorrow.
The papers will checked by the teacher tomorrow.
The papers would be checked by the teacher tomorrow.
The papers will be checked by the teacher tomorrow.
explanation: The simple future passive is “will be + past participle”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Who wrote this letter?”
o: By whom is this letter written?
By whom this letter was written?
By whom was this letter written?
Who was this letter written?
explanation: In the passive, “who” becomes “by whom”, the question keeps inverted order, and the simple past gives “was…written”.

subject: English
q: Change into passive voice: “Close the door.”
o: The door should closed.
The door is closed.
Let the door closed.
Let the door be closed.
explanation: An imperative sentence becomes passive with “Let + object + be + past participle”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The police had arrested the thief before sunrise.”
o: The thief had arrested by the police before sunrise.
The thief had been arrested by the police before sunrise.
The thief was arrested by the police before sunrise.
The thief has been arrested by the police before sunrise.
explanation: The past perfect passive is “had been + past participle”.

subject: English
q: Change into passive voice: “They were repairing the road when we passed.”
o: The road was being repaired when we passed.
The road was repaired when we passed.
The road had been repaired when we passed.
The road is being repaired when we passed.
explanation: The past continuous passive is “was/were being + past participle”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct passive voice of: “People speak Punjabi in many parts of Pakistan.”
o: Punjabi is speaking in many parts of Pakistan.
Punjabi has spoken in many parts of Pakistan.
Punjabi is spoken in many parts of Pakistan.
Punjabi was spoken in many parts of Pakistan.
explanation: The simple present passive is “is/are + past participle”; the general agent “people” is dropped.

subject: English
q: Change into passive voice: “Did the manager sign the cheque?”
o: Did the cheque sign by the manager?
Was the cheque signed by the manager?
Is the cheque signed by the manager?
Was the cheque sign by the manager?
explanation: A simple past question with “did” becomes “Was/Were + subject + past participle?” in the passive.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The chairman gave me a prize.”
o: I am given a prize by the chairman.
I had given a prize by the chairman.
I was give a prize by the chairman.
I was given a prize by the chairman.
explanation: With two objects, the indirect object (“me” → “I”) can become the subject: “I was given a prize”.

subject: English
q: Change into passive voice: “You must obey the rules.”
o: The rules must be obeyed.
The rules must be obey.
The rules must have been obeyed.
The rules must obeyed.
explanation: A modal passive is “modal + be + past participle”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The storm destroyed hundreds of houses.”
o: Hundreds of houses was destroyed by the storm.
Hundreds of houses are destroyed by the storm.
Hundreds of houses were destroyed by the storm.
Hundreds of houses had destroyed by the storm.
explanation: The plural subject “houses” takes “were” in the simple past passive.

subject: English
q: Change into passive voice: “The farmers are harvesting the wheat.”
o: The wheat was being harvested by the farmers.
The wheat is being harvested by the farmers.
The wheat is harvested by the farmers.
The wheat are being harvested by the farmers.
explanation: The present continuous passive with a singular subject is “is being + past participle”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct passive voice of: “We will have completed the work by June.”
o: The work will have been completed by us by June.
The work will be completed by us by June.
The work will have completed by us by June.
The work would have been completed by us by June.
explanation: The future perfect passive is “will have been + past participle”.

subject: English
q: Change into passive voice: “Why did he insult you?”
o: Why are you insulted by him?
Why did you insulted by him?
Why was you insulted by him?
Why were you insulted by him?
explanation: The question word stays first; “did…insult” becomes “were…insulted”, agreeing with “you”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct active voice of: “The match was won by our team.”
o: Our team has won the match.
Our team had been won the match.
Our team won the match.
Our team wins the match.
explanation: The simple past passive “was won” becomes the simple past active “won”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct active voice of: “The letter has been posted by my brother.”
o: My brother has been posted the letter.
My brother posted the letter.
My brother has posted the letter.
My brother had posted the letter.
explanation: The present perfect passive “has been posted” becomes the present perfect active “has posted”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “I am busy.”
o: He said that I am busy.
He said that he was busy.
He said that he is busy.
He said that he had been busy.
explanation: After a past reporting verb, “I” becomes “he” and the simple present “am” becomes the simple past “was”.

subject: English
q: Change into indirect speech: She said, “I have finished my work.”
o: She said that she had finished her work.
She told that she had finished her work.
She said that she had finish her work.
She said that she has finished her work.
explanation: The present perfect becomes the past perfect; “told” needs an object, so “said” is used here.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The teacher said to the boys, “Do not make a noise.”
o: The teacher told the boys that do not make a noise.
The teacher said the boys not to make a noise.
The teacher told the boys don’t make a noise.
The teacher told the boys not to make a noise.
explanation: A negative command is reported with “told/ordered + object + not to + verb”.

subject: English
q: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, “Where do you live?”
o: He asked me where do I live.
He asked me where did I live.
He said to me where I lived.
He asked me where I lived.
explanation: A reported question uses “asked”, statement word order and a backshifted tense.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said to me, “Will you help me?”
o: She asked me if I will help her.
She asked me if would I help her.
She asked me if I would help her.
She said me if I would help her.
explanation: A yes/no question is reported with “asked…if/whether”; “will” becomes “would” and the word order becomes that of a statement.

subject: English
q: Change into indirect speech: He said, “I will go to Karachi tomorrow.”
o: He said that he would went to Karachi the next day.
He said that he would go to Karachi the next day.
He said that he would go to Karachi the previous day.
He said that he will go to Karachi the next day.
explanation: “Will” becomes “would” and “tomorrow” becomes “the next day”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The teacher said, “The earth moves round the sun.”
o: The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moving round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher told that the earth moves round the sun.
explanation: A universal truth normally keeps its present tense in reported speech; “told” would need an object.

subject: English
q: Change into indirect speech: He said, “Alas! I have lost my purse.”
o: He exclaimed with sorrow that he has lost his purse.
He exclaimed with sorrow that he had lost his purse.
He exclaimed with sorrow that alas he had lost his purse.
He exclaimed with sorrow that he had lost my purse.
explanation: The interjection is replaced by a reporting phrase (“exclaimed with sorrow”), the present perfect becomes the past perfect, and pronouns change.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: The officer said to the clerk, “Please bring the file.”
o: The officer requested the clerk to bring the file.
The officer requested the clerk bringing the file.
The officer requested to the clerk to bring the file.
The officer requested the clerk that bring the file.
explanation: A polite command with “please” is reported with “requested + object + to-infinitive”.

subject: English
q: Change into indirect speech: She said, “I was reading a novel.”
o: She said that I had been reading a novel.
She said that she had been read a novel.
She said that she had been reading a novel.
She said that she has been reading a novel.
explanation: The past continuous is backshifted to the past perfect continuous “had been reading”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “Let us wait for the bus.”
o: He suggested that let us wait for the bus.
He told that they should wait for the bus.
He suggested them to wait for the bus.
He suggested that they should wait for the bus.
explanation: “Let us” expressing a proposal is reported with “suggested that…should”.

subject: English
q: Change into indirect speech: “Are you coming to the wedding?” Ayesha asked me.
o: Ayesha told me whether I was coming to the wedding.
Ayesha asked me whether I was coming to the wedding.
Ayesha asked me whether was I coming to the wedding.
Ayesha asked me that whether I was coming to the wedding.
explanation: A yes/no question is reported with “whether”, statement word order and a backshifted tense, without “that”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, “I can swim across the river.”
o: He said that I could swim across the river.
He said that he could swam across the river.
He said that he could swim across the river.
He said that he can swimming across the river.
explanation: “Can” becomes “could”, followed by the base verb, and “I” becomes “he”.

subject: English
q: Change into indirect speech: She said, “My father is ill.”
o: She said that her father is being ill.
She said that my father was ill.
She said me that her father was ill.
She said that her father was ill.
explanation: “My” becomes “her” and “is” becomes “was”; “said” takes no personal object.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said to his servant, “Go and fetch some water.”
o: He ordered his servant to go and fetch some water.
He ordered his servant that go and fetch some water.
He ordered to his servant to go and fetch some water.
He ordered his servant going and fetching some water.
explanation: A command is reported with “ordered + object + to-infinitive”.

subject: English
q: Change into indirect speech: The student said, “Sir, may I come in?”
o: The student respectfully asked the teacher if he might come in.
The student respectfully asked the teacher that may he come in.
The student respectfully asked the teacher if might he come in.
The student said sir if he might come in.
explanation: “Sir” becomes “respectfully asked the teacher”, the question takes “if” with statement order, and “may” becomes “might”.
